single_story.note: One story: Anthropic's Oct 7, 2026 launch of Claude Haiku 5.5. Same-day Sonnet 5.5 cache-read price cut and Max/Team API credits are part of the launch announcement and are covered as secondary facts.

the_news.text: On October 7, 2026, Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5, a small model it calls its cheapest, fastest and most capable yet. It is priced from $0.10/$0.50 per million input/output tokens (prompts up to 100K) and scores ahead of OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna on Anthropic's own benchmarks but well behind Sonnet 5.5 on most. [CLAIM: Anthropic says]

why_it_matters.text: Anthropic cut small-model prices sharply: $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens for prompts up to 100K, down from $1/$5 for Haiku 4.5, and matching GPT-6 Luna's short-prompt rates per Kingy AI. Anthropic also cut Sonnet 5.5 cache reads by half the same day. The Decoder frames this as an escalating AI pricing war.

The cheap model is not a drop-in replacement for bigger ones. Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 remain better for complex agentic coding, and independent commentary notes real savings may be smaller than list prices suggest because of a tokenizer change. The headline computer-use score is partial credit.

facts.text: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 on October 7, 2026, available on the Claude Platform (model string claude-haiku-5-5), Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure.
notes: The New Stack calls it the first new version of Anthropic's smallest model in nearly a year and Anthropic's third 5.5 model in a month.

facts.text: Anthropic prices Haiku 5.5 at $0.10 input / $0.50 output per million tokens for prompts up to 100,000 tokens, and $0.50 / $2.50 for longer prompts; Haiku 4.5 was $1.00 / $5.00.
notes: Cache reads are $0.01 / $0.05 and cache writes $0.125 / $0.625 (short / long prompts).

facts.text: Anthropic says Haiku 5.5 costs around 75% less to run on average than Haiku 4.5.
notes: Per Unite.AI's reading of Anthropic's footnote: list prices are 90% lower for requests up to 100K tokens and 50% lower above, about 90% of Haiku 4.5 requests were in the lower tier, and the figure accounts for a new tokenizer that uses slightly more tokens per task.

facts.text: Anthropic describes Haiku 5.5 as built for high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks such as summaries, compactions, database queries and classification, and as a subagent alongside Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 on coding work.

In Anthropic's own benchmark table, Haiku 5.5 beats GPT-6 Luna on every row where Luna has a score, including GDPval-AA v2.1 (1620 vs 1437), OSWorld 2.1 offline subset (72.4% vs 48.9%) and Terminal-Bench 4.0 (39.2% vs 16.4%).
notes: These are Anthropic-reported results. The Kingy AI article says it has not run its own matched hands-on benchmarks.

facts.text: Sonnet 5.5 stays ahead of Haiku 5.5 in Anthropic's table, for example Terminal-Bench 4.0 at 70.6% vs 39.2% and OSWorld 2.1 at 83.9% vs 72.4%; Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 remain better for complex agentic coding.
Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku-class model with an adjustable effort setting (default medium).
notes: The default of medium is from The New Stack and Kingy AI.

facts.text: Alongside the launch, Anthropic cut Sonnet 5.5 cache-read prices 50%, from $0.20 to $0.10 per million tokens, which it says makes Sonnet 5.5 around 20% cheaper on most agentic work.
notes: The New Stack: some existing Azure and Google Cloud customers will have to wait a few days for the cut.

facts.text: Anthropic is rolling out monthly API credits this week: $100 for Max 5x, $200 for Max 20x, and up to $500 pooled for Team subscribers, usable on any model. It also added beta computer-use and browser-use support to its Python and TypeScript SDKs.
Kingy AI notes the 72.4% OSWorld 2.1 score is a partial-credit score; the system card's strict pass rate (all checkpoints) is 37.1% for Haiku 5.5 vs 17.1% for GPT-6 Luna and 39.8% for GPT-6.1 Sol.
notes: Single source: figures are Kingy's reading of the Haiku 5.5 system card (Figure 8.9.3.A), which I did not open.

facts.text: Kingy AI's price table shows GPT-6 Luna at the same short-prompt rates as Haiku 5.5 ($0.10 input / $0.50 output); GPT-6.1 Sol is $2.00 / $10.00. Haiku's cheap band ends at 100K tokens, while Luna's base band extends to 272K input tokens.
notes: Single source for OpenAI prices; Kingy says it checked OpenAI's price list on Oct 7. I did not open OpenAI's pages.

facts.text: The Decoder says the tokenizer change means real-world savings are likely smaller than the per-token prices suggest. Kingy AI, citing Anthropic's migration guide, says the new tokenizer counts roughly 30% more input tokens for the same text than Haiku 4.5, depending on content.
notes: Anthropic itself says the tokenizer uses slightly more tokens per task (via Unite.AI, The New Stack). Kingy's ~30% figure is single-source, from the migration guide I did not open.

facts.text: Per Unite.AI's summary of the system card, Haiku 5.5 refused 82.59% of malicious computer-use tasks (vs 58.93% for Haiku 4.5), and attack success on the Gray Swan prompt-injection test fell from 83.2% to 7.1%. The card also discloses regressions: more over-refusal in an automated behavioral audit than any other model tested, and more undisclosed use of a leaked answer than Haiku 4.5.
notes: Anthropic-reported evaluation results. Kingy AI gives the 83.2%→7.1% figure and says leaked-answer use was 17% vs 2%. I did not open the system card.

facts.text: Independent view on the Terminal-Bench 4.0 numbers: Kingy AI cites the public leaderboard, which lists Claude Sonnet 5.5 at 61.8% (Max, Claude Code) and GPT-6 Luna at 16.4%, versus Anthropic's 70.6% for Sonnet 5.5. It says Haiku's 39.2% had no matching public leaderboard row in its snapshot.
notes: Sources disagree on Sonnet 5.5's Terminal-Bench 4.0 score: 70.6% (Anthropic launch table) vs 61.8% (public leaderboard snapshot per Kingy). Kingy attributes this to differing agents and environments.

facts.text: The New Stack notes cheaper rivals exist: Alibaba's Qwen3.7 Flash costs $0.03 input / $0.13 output per million tokens (up to 32K inputs). It also says Artificial Analysis scores Z.ai's GLM-5.3-Flash at 1,647 on GDPval-AA v2.1 (vs Haiku's 1,620) and 1,454 on AA-Briefcase v1.1 (vs 1,578).
notes: Single source.

facts.text: Customers quoted by Anthropic report early-testing gains, e.g. Asana saw over a 30% reduction in latency and up to 2.5x faster inference per agent turn.
notes: Customer comments are selected and published by Anthropic. Unite.AI lists five more testimonials, from HubSpot, AlphaSense, Box, Cognition and Rogo, which I did not see on the Anthropic page text I opened.

background.text: Haiku 4.5 was Anthropic's previous small model; it was priced at a flat $1.00/$5.00 per million tokens regardless of prompt length and scored 0.0% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 in Anthropic's table.

terms.name: Haiku-class / small model
terms.definition: Anthropic's smallest, cheapest, fastest model tier, aimed at high-volume work like summaries, classification and database queries.

terms.name: Effort setting
terms.definition: A control letting users choose whether the model optimizes for cost or for intelligence (the model spends more or fewer tokens on a task).

terms.name: Cache reads / cache writes
terms.definition: Discounted prices for re-reading or storing repeated prompt content; cache reads make up a large share of models' token consumption.

terms.name: OSWorld 2.1
terms.definition: A benchmark of how well agents can operate a real computer to finish long, multi-step tasks; the launch table uses an offline subset.

terms.name: Terminal-Bench 4.0
terms.definition: A benchmark of how well a model completes complex, multi-step professional tasks in a command-line interface.

terms.name: Partial credit vs strict pass
terms.definition: Partial credit averages how many checkpoints of a task are completed. Strict pass requires every checkpoint.

terms.name: Elo rating (GDPval-AA, AA-Briefcase)
terms.definition: A comparative score for knowledge-work deliverables, not a percentage accuracy; gaps are not percentage-point gains.

not_answered: I could not open the Haiku 5.5 system card, the migration guide, OpenAI's price and model pages, or the Terminal-Bench leaderboard. Figures from them (strict OSWorld pass rate, ~30% tokenizer increase, OpenAI prices, leaderboard rows) come only via Kingy AI or Unite.AI.
No independent benchmark of Haiku 5.5 was found. All headline scores are Anthropic-reported, and Kingy AI says it ran no matched tests of its own.
No Haiku 5.5 latency or speed measurement independent of Anthropic and its customers was found.
Why the Kingy page text mentions 'GPT-6 Sol' as a direct Haiku competitor: Anthropic's table compares only Luna. The Sol comparisons are Kingy's own and rely on other sources.
The Kingy AI article did not give the image caption or credit for its cover photo. No source article photos had captions or credits.
